findings.evidence: Adding the lockdownMode record component changes the public canonical constructor from the previous 12-argument CreateExamDraftRequest and 13-argument PatchExamDraftRequest signatures. The only overloads added accept the older reduced forms that predate selectedSkills/maxRetriesPerStudent; no overload preserves the immediately previous full constructor signatures.
findings.why_it_matters: Existing Java callers compiled against the canonical draft DTO constructors will fail to compile even though the phase explicitly requires source-compatible DTO constructors and optional JSON compatibility.
findings.required_action: Add public overloads matching the pre-change full CreateExamDraftRequest and PatchExamDraftRequest constructor signatures, delegating to the new canonical constructor with lockdownMode=null. Keep the reduced legacy overloads as well.

findings.evidence: toPolicy(policy, examMode) always calls resolveEffectiveLockdownMode(..., true), so every null lockdown value is treated as legacy. The phase resolver explicitly supports legacyState=false to fail closed for non-legacy null state, but the response and entitlement paths never select that branch.
findings.why_it_matters: A newly created or corrupted canonical session with a missing lockdown value can be returned as if it had a valid mode-derived policy, bypassing the phase requirement that non-legacy null state fail closed before response mapping and snapshot pinning.
findings.required_action: Carry an explicit legacy/non-legacy state decision into the session boundary and pass it to the resolver. Canonical drafts and persisted sessions known to be canonical must use legacyState=false; only identified legacy rows may receive the mode-aware compatibility default. Ensure the same resolved value is used before entitlement and snapshot pinning.

findings.evidence: The default embedded policy changed from ExamPolicy.mockTestDefault() to ExamPolicy.realExamDefault(). Canonical create and update flows already assign an explicit policy, so this domain-default change is not required to implement lockdownMode and affects any other construction path that does not immediately overwrite policy.
findings.why_it_matters: It silently changes the behavior of legacy or alternate session construction paths during rollout, conflicting with the phase constraint to leave the legacy route behavior unchanged and creating a stricter policy without an explicit exam-mode resolution.
findings.required_action: Restore the pre-change mockTestDefault() field default, or replace it with an explicitly documented compatibility strategy that proves every construction path sets policy before use. Do not use a global real-exam default as a substitute for mode-aware resolution.

findings.evidence: The comment says ExamPolicy.forMode()/backfillLegacyDefaults() always set all 5 policy fields together, but the current backfillLegacyDefaults implementation intentionally leaves lockdownMode null for mode-aware resolution.
findings.why_it_matters: The stale statement makes the null-lockdown compatibility design harder to reason about and contradicts the implementation immediately being reviewed.
findings.required_action: Update the comment to distinguish the four legacy backfilled fields from the intentionally mode-resolved lockdown field.

findings.evidence: patchPolicy dereferences session.getPolicy() before checking for an incomplete/null embedded policy. A malformed legacy row can therefore produce a NullPointerException rather than the stable fail-closed policy error. This dereference predates the Phase 1 diff.
findings.why_it_matters: The phase defines explicit null and fail-closed policy behavior, but this existing policy-patch boundary still has an uncontrolled failure path for malformed persisted state.
findings.required_action: Track for the policy-boundary hardening follow-up; if Phase 1 remediation touches this path, convert the null/incomplete state to the owning stable DomainException without changing partial-update semantics.
